title: Co-evolving networks for opinion and social dynamics in agent-based models

key_points.claim: Introduces a stochastic ABM where opinion and social position co-evolve. Agent mobility in a social space depends on social and opinion similarity. Opinion updates depend on social neighbours.
key_points.evidence_quote: Agents' mobility in a social space is governed by both their social and opinion similarity with others; and similarly, opinion dynamics is driven by the opinions of agents in their social vicinity.

key_points.claim: Model is formulated as coupled SDEs. It is used to study when consensus or echo chambers emerge.
key_points.evidence_quote: We formulate our model with a system of coupled stochastic differential equations (SDEs) and study which factors drive the emergence of consensus, or alternatively echo chambers

key_points.claim: Prior adaptive-network models rewire by opinion similarity. This tends to cause fragmentation and prevents global consensus.
key_points.evidence_quote: This mechanism is shown to hinder the system's ability to reach global consensus, but rather leads to fragmentation

key_points.claim: Gap identified: most ABMs ignore intrinsic social dynamics and treat influence as one-directional.
key_points.evidence_quote: most such ABMs neglect incorporating the intrinsic social dynamics of agents, a key factor influencing social interaction patterns

key_points.claim: Model is applied to General Social Survey data on political identity and views on government issues.
key_points.evidence_quote: we apply it to General Social Survey data on political identity and public opinion regarding governmental issues

reliability_notes: Only the first part of the paper (abstract and introduction) was read. The full text was returned by the fetch, but I did not read the results sections. The paper is an arXiv preprint and may not be peer-reviewed. It covers opinion dynamics and social networks in ABMs, not artificial societies in general.
